title: Federal learning method and device based on cluster training and gradient sparsity

pse.problem: Inefficiencies and privacy concerns in traditional federated learning due to data imbalance, low communication efficiency, and non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data among clients
pse.solution_function: Addresses the problem by proposing a federated learning method based on cluster training and gradient sparsity that improves local model updates and global model aggregation in Non-IID scenarios, reducing oscillations during training and enhancing privacy protection.
pse.solution_structure: Includes multiple clients (Client1 to Client n) for distributed data processing, a central server for model aggregation, and sparsity constraints to control the importance of each client's update in the global model
pse.solution_implementation: Clients perform local training using their own datasets, sending updates to the central server. The central server aggregates updates from clients, applies cluster training, and implements gradient sparsity to minimize the impact of noisy or small-data clients on the final global model.
pse.effect: Improves communication efficiency by reducing the amount of data transmitted between clients and the central server, enhances privacy protection by not exposing user data, and maintains comparable accuracy to centralized training (CL) in Non-IID scenarios
